acts.lead:
Write a news article based on the following facts. Write an appropriate
headline for your article.

The Philippines will host the APEC Summit in 2015.
“We welcome the offer of the People’s Republic of China, the Philippines, and
Peru to host APEC in 2014, 2015, and 2016 respectively,” said the 2012
Vladivostok Leaders’ Declaration. “We welcome the invitation from the
President of Indonesia to meet again in Bali in 2013,” it added.
The 21 APEC members agreed to end by 2015 raising new barriers for the
following: investment, trade in goods & services, imposing new export
restrictions, implementing the World Trade Organization (WTO) measures
with effects to protect members in the face of the global economic downturn.
For food security, APEC member economies reaffirmed its commitment to a
10% improvement in supply-chain performance by 2015, in terms of
reduction of time, cost, and uncertainty of moving goods and services
through the Asia-Pacific region.
The representatives of the summit had a sumptuous dinner with Cornish
Crab Salad on Lemon Blini, Pressed Duck Terrine with Fruit Chutney,
Roulade of Goat Cheese with Caramelized Walnuts, Assortment of Palmiers
and Cheese Straws, Scottish Smoked Salmon Rose on Beetroot Blini,
Miniature Watercress and Asparagus Tart and Quail Eggs with Celery Salt.
The environment was given focus with the leaders expressing concern on
trafficking of endangered and protected wildlife species. A commitment was
directed at strengthening efforts in combating illegal trade of environmental
resources.
Other commitments for strengthening are as follows: drive against terrorism;
improve travel and tourism for job creation and disaster management.
Members of the APEC are Australia, Brunei Darussalam, Canada, Chile,
China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Republic of Korea, Malaysia, Mexico,
New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Peru, Philippines, Russia, Singapore,
Taiwan, Thailand, United States of America, and Vietnam.

The news was formally announced at the end of the 20th Asia Pacific
Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting, Vladivostok,
Russia

kanilang probinsya,” Presidential spokesperson Harry Roque said on state-
run PTV4.
(The President ordered DOLE, OWWA and DOH to make sure that the
24,000 OFWs awaiting their COVID-19 test result are sent home within
week.)
According to Roque, the President said the concerned agencies may utilize
all government resources to ferry the OFWs back to their provinces.
Duterte also said there is a need to boost coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-

of COVID test results
By: Krissy Aguilar - Reporter/@KAguilarINQ        INQUIRER.net / 07:19 AM
May 25, 2020
MANILA, Philippines — President Rodrigo Duterte has given the Department
of Labor and Employment (DOLE), Overseas Workers Welfare Administration
(OWWA) and the Department of Health (DOH) a week to send home some
24,000 overseas Filipino workers (OFWs) who are awaiting their coronavirus
disease 2019 (COVID- 19) results in various quarantine facilities,
Malacañang said Monday.
“Inutusan po ng ating Presidente and DOLE, OWWA, at ang DOH na meron
lamang silang isang linggo para masiguro na lahat po ng 24,000 na OFWs
na kapatid nating mga Pilipino na nagaantay ng resulta ay mapauwi sa kani
kanilang probinsya,” Presidential spokesperson Harry Roque said on state-
run PTV4.
(The President ordered DOLE, OWWA and DOH to make sure that the
24,000 OFWs awaiting their COVID-19 test result are sent home within
week.)
According to Roque, the President said the concerned agencies may utilize
all government resources to ferry the OFWs back to their provinces.
Duterte also said there is a need to boost coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-
19) testing nationwide.
“Nagsabi din ang ating Pangulo na kinakailangan palakasin na ang PCR
[polymerase chain reaction] testing sa iba’t ibang lugar ng Pilipinas, hindi
lamang dito sa Metro Manila nang sa ganon, pupuwede na silang umuwi
diretso sa kanilang mga probinsya ang       mga OFWs at doon na sila
magpakuha ng PCT COVID-19 test,” he said.
(The President also saw the need to beef up PCR testing nationwide and not
only in Metro Manila. That way, OFWs can be tested in their home
provinces.)
A number of repatriated OFWs have complained that they have been
confined to quarantine facilities beyond the mandatory 14-day isolation
period due to the delay in the release of their COVID-19 test
results.

Focus on how the editorial presents opinions, supports claims, addresses counterarguments, and persuades readers to take action.
acts.lead:
Instruction:
Read the editorial carefully. Analyze the writer’s stand, arguments, evidence,
and overall structure. Then, answer the guide questions in complete
sentences. Focus on how the editorial presents opinions, supports claims,
addresses counterarguments, and persuades readers to take action.

Should Schools Adopt a Later Start Time?

Many high school students struggle with fatigue, poor concentration,
and declining mental health, largely because school starts too early.
Research shows that teenagers have different sleep cycles than adults and
naturally stay up later at night. It is time for schools to adopt later start
times to improve students’ health, academic performance, and overall well-
being.

First, early school hours negatively impact students’ physical and
mental health. Sleep deprivation can lead to stress, anxiety, poor immunity,
and reduced cognitive functioning. By starting school later, students are
more likely to get the recommended 8–10 hours of sleep, leading to better
mood, energy, and focus in class.

Second, academic performance improves when students are well-
rested. Studies indicate that schools with later start times have higher
attendance rates, better test scores, and increased engagement in lessons.
When students are alert, they can absorb and retain information more
effectively, resulting in stronger academic outcomes.

Some argue that changing the start time may interfere with after-
school activities, sports, and parental schedules. While adjustments are
necessary, the benefits of better sleep and mental health far outweigh the
logistical challenges. Schools can modify schedules gradually or provide
flexible extracurricular timings to accommodate students and families.

In conclusion, shifting school start times is a simple yet powerful way
to support teenagers’ physical health, mental well-being, and academic
success. Educators, parents, and policymakers must work together to make
this change. It’s time to prioritize students’ needs and give them the rest
they deserve.

Guide Questions:

items.text: What is the writer’s stance on school start times, and how is it clearly expressed in the editorial?
Identify at least two reasons the writer gives to support the claim that schools should start later.
How does the writer acknowledge opposing views, and why is this important in editorial writing?
Which part of the editorial functions as the “call to action,” and how does it persuade the reader to act?
How does the structure (introduction, body, counterargument, conclusion) enhance the clarity and persuasiveness of the editorial?
What kind of evidence does the writer use to strengthen their argument? (e.g., studies, statistics, logical reasoning)
If you were to add one more reason to support the editorial, what would it be, and why?

acts.lead:
Write an explanatory essay about the science behind one sports-related
topic, such as:
    How muscles work during a sprint
    Why proper warm-up prevents injury
    How reaction time affects performance in sports
    The role of nutrition and hydration in athletes
    Introduction:
o     Introduce your chosen topic.
o     Explain why it is important in sports.
   Body:
o     Use clear, factual explanations.
o     Include at least one simple diagram idea (you can
describe it instead of drawing):
   Example: “A labeled diagram could show the
major leg muscles used in sprinting.”
o     Use correct but understandable terms (e.g., stamina,
coordination, lactic acid).
   Conclusion:
o     Summarize the main points.
o     End with practical advice for student athletes.
Length: 450–550 words
Skills: Expository writing, using academic tone, explaining
concepts clearly.

items.text: Main caption/post (120–180 words) o   Encourage students to join a sport or be more active. o   Mention benefits: physical health, mental health, friendships, discipline, etc. o   Use a friendly, motivational tone.

lessons.label: Activity 16

acts.lead:
Human Interest Story “A Day in the Life”
Step-by-Step Instructions:

items.text: Choose a subject: Select a person in your school or community whose daily life or experiences are interesting. Examples: a teacher, a school staff member, a local artist, or a peer with a unique hobby.
Plan your approach: Think of 5–7 questions to ask during an interview, focusing on their daily routine, challenges, achievements, and personal interests.
Observe: Spend time observing your subject in their environment. Take detailed notes about their actions, expressions, and interactions.
Conduct an interview: Use your prepared questions. Record or write down their responses verbatim to include direct quotes in your article.

Write your feature article (400–500 words): o    Lead: Begin with an engaging anecdote or scene from their day. o    Body: Share their story, including quotes, descriptive details, and personal insights. o    Conclusion: Reflect on what makes this person’s life inspiring, interesting, or unique. EXAMPLE: Mr. Daniel, the school janitor Lead: Every morning at 5:30 a.m., while most of the town is still asleep, Mr. Daniel is already sweeping the empty corridors of Riverside High School. The faint smell of disinfectant fills the air as he hums a soft tune, preparing the school for another day of learning. Body: Mr. Daniel has worked at Riverside High for over 15 years. “I enjoy seeing the students smile when the school is clean,” he says with a warm grin. His day begins with sweeping and mopping floors, followed by restocking classrooms and checking that all facilities are in order. Despite his busy schedule, he always finds time to greet students by name. “It’s the small things that make my day worthwhile,” he explains. Outside work, Mr. Daniel volunteers at the local community center, helping children with homework and organizing weekend sports activities. Conclusion: Mr. Daniel’s dedication reminds everyone that every role in the school community matters. Through his hard work and kindness, he quietly makes Riverside High a brighter place for students and staff alike.

lessons.label: Activity 17

acts.lead:
Trend Feature “The Rising Craze”
Step-by-Step Instructions:

items.text: Select a trend: Identify a current trend among teenagers (e.g., social media challenge, fashion style, hobby, or app).
Research: Use the internet, social media, and news articles to gather information about the trend. Note its origin, popularity, and impact.
Interview peers: Ask classmates or friends why they follow this trend and what they like about it. Record at least 2–3 quotes.

Plan your article: Create an outline: o    Introduction: Hook the reader with a fun fact, question, or statistic about the trend. o    Body: Explain what the trend is, why it is popular, and who participates. Include quotes and interesting details. o    Impact: Discuss how it affects teens or society (positively or negatively). o    Conclusion: Summarize the trend’s importance or speculate about its future.
Write your feature article (400–500 words): Use clear, engaging language and maintain a friendly, lively tone.

Edit and polish: Check for grammar, smooth flow, and correct facts. Make sure quotes and data are accurate. EXAMPLE: DIY Resin Art Lead: Over the past year, a colorful wave of creativity has taken over social media: DIY resin art. From glittery keychains to miniature landscapes, teenagers are turning their free time into artistic masterpieces. Body: Resin art involves mixing resin with pigments, glitter, and molds to create small decorative items. Teens like 16-year-old Maya explain why they love it: “It’s relaxing, and I love seeing the final product shine.” The trend has gained attention on Instagram and TikTok, with thousands of posts under #ResinArt. Schools and online communities now host workshops where beginners can learn to craft their own resin pieces. Experts note that resin art encourages creativity and patience, giving teenagers a productive way to spend their time. Impact: While resin art is mostly positive, some teens spend large amounts on supplies, which can be costly. However, many view it as a hobby that boosts confidence and skills. Conclusion: From glitter-filled coasters to custom jewelry, DIY resin art shows how a simple craft can inspire a generation of young creators. As more teens experiment with colors and shapes, the trend is likely to grow even further.

lessons.label: Activity 18

acts.lead:
Place Feature – “Hidden Gems in Our Community”
Step-by-Step Instructions:

items.text: Choose a location: Find a lesser-known or interesting place in your community or school (park, café, library corner, historical site).
Visit and observe: Spend 15–30 minutes noting details about the surroundings, atmosphere, people, sounds, smells, and activities.
Talk to people: If possible, ask visitors or staff about their experiences at the place. Record at least 1–2 quotes.

Plan your article: Organize your observations: o    Lead: Open with a vivid description or scene-setting that immediately immerses the reader. o    Body: Describe the place in detail, include quotes, history (if relevant), and why it is unique. o    Conclusion: Suggest why readers should visit or appreciate this hidden gem.
Write your feature article (400–500 words): Use descriptive language, imagery, and personification. Make the reader feel as if they are visiting the place themselves.

Revise and proofread: Ensure your article flow well, has correct grammar, and creates a; strong impression of the location. Example: Maple Grove Park Lead: Tucked behind the main road in downtown Oakville, Maple Grove Park is a serene escape from the city’s hustle. The soft rustling of leaves and the scent of blooming flowers greet visitors as they step onto winding cobblestone paths. Body: The Park is dotted with wooden benches, perfect for reading or quiet reflection. Children play near the small fountain, while joggers circle the walking trails. “I come here every morning; it’s peaceful and refreshing,” says local resident Mr. Cruz. Historically, Maple Grove Park was established in 1920 and still retains its century-old oak trees. Birdsong fills the air, and butterflies often flutter past the flowerbeds, adding to the park’s charm. Conclusion: Whether you’re seeking a quiet spot to read, a place to exercise, or a peaceful escape from the busy city, Maple Grove Park is a hidden gem worth exploring. It proves that sometimes, the most beautiful places are the ones we least expect.

Write a short weather report about the information provided below.  Greeting  Today’s weather  Temperature  A simple forecast (e.g. “Sunny this afternoon”, “cloudy skies”)  Advice for listeners (e.g. “Don’t forget your jacket!”) Example: “Good day, everyone! Write a short school announcement about an upcoming event (field trip, contest, club meeting), or a reminder (uniform, deadlines, project submissions).
